chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Hazhaz from Ali ibn al-Sari who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made the sustenance of the believers from where they did not expect, and that is because when the servant does not know the source of his sustenance, his supplication increases.'

key_terms.لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا: From where they did not expect or calculate

ai.seo_question: Why does a believer's supplication increase when they are unaware of the source of their sustenance?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*'s chapter on earnings, this narration highlights the spiritual benefit of *ghayb* (unseen nature) of provision, where uncertainty fosters continuous *du'a*. This aligns with the Shia scholarly view that reliance on God (*tawakkul*) is strengthened when one does not fixate on specific worldly means, thereby maintaining a state of active supplication and humility.
